priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Fidelity
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Correct: adherence to required steps is a fidelity measure.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Adoption
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Adoption measures initial uptake, not adherence.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Acceptability
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Acceptability measures stakeholder agreeableness, not adherence.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Feasibility
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Feasibility measures whether implementation can be carried out in the setting, not adherence.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Document the agreed medicine action and reassess nausea and intake against the goal
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Correct: evaluates both action taken and actual symptom/intake response.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Count completed reviews without recording subsequent actions or patient response
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Completed review counts show process completion, not patient benefit.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Compare the number of laboratory results before and after the review
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Availability of lab results alone does not establish the proposed intervention response.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Report the admission nutrition-risk score without reassessing the barrier
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: An admission screen alone does not evaluate the current barrier or response.

retainedQuestions.sourceAndApplicationScope: NICECG32 1.1.3-4,1.5.1,Table1 intake/GI symptoms/drugtherapy/goals;Proctor conceptualframework;NaS case application

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: A useful interval detects meaningful benefit or harm in time to inform the next decision
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Correct: interval should permit useful benefit/safety reassessment.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: The discharge review interval is sufficient for every inpatient because support is prescribed
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Discharge-only review ignores initial inpatient monitoring.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: A single fixed interval permits comparison even when the patient becomes unstable
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Unchanging interval during instability ignores risk adaptation.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Normal baseline tests justify keeping the longest interval throughout initiation
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Baseline normality does not establish continued safety after initiation.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Outcome: intake improves toward the goal; process: scheduled intake records are completed
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Correct: improved intake is a patient result;record completion is a process.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Outcome: a medicine review is documented; process: nausea resolves
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Reverses documentation process and nausea outcome.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Outcome: the feed order is signed; process: the patient tolerates feeding
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Reverses order-signing process and feeding-tolerance outcome.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Outcome: the assessment checklist is completed; process: intake meets the agreed goal
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Reverses checklist process and intake-goal outcome.

retainedQuestions.sourceAndApplicationScope: Proctor Background/conceptualframework distinguishes clinical from implementation outcomes;NICETable1 intake/goal/drugtherapy monitoring;NaS concrete examples

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Show the source findings, chosen criteria, confounders and uncertainty, then link the proposed action to a measurable follow-up plan
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Correct: evidence,criteria,uncertainty and measured response can be reviewed.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Use a screening score to establish the diagnosis without assessing its underlying findings
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: A screen alone supplies risk information, not an independently established diagnosis.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: List measurements without stating how they support the problem or intervention
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Unconnected measurements do not explain the decision.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Document the intervention as effective before measuring the patient response
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: An intended benefit is not an observed response.

retainedQuestions.sourceAndApplicationScope: NICECG32 1.2screening,1.3indications,1.4prescription and1.5goal/response review;NaS evidence-transparent reasoning application;no new GLIMthreshold certification

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Review timing and competing causes, agree a safe adjustment with the prescriber if appropriate, and reassess nausea and intake
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Correct: investigate plausible contribution,review indication/alternatives andmeasure response.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Declare the medicine causal from timing alone and stop it without reviewing its indication
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Temporal association alone is insufficient to assign causation or stop therapy indiscriminately.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Continue the nutrition plan without assessing whether the suspected medicine can be changed safely
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Leaves the possible barrier and safe adjustment unassessed.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Change the medicine with the prescriber but omit any assessment of symptoms or intake afterward
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: An action without response assessment leaves benefit unmeasured.

retainedQuestions.sourceAndApplicationScope: NICECG32 1.1.3-4,Table1 GI symptoms/drugtherapy/goals,1.6.4drugreview in dysphagia;NaS nonspecificmedicine-barrier case application

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Arrange baseline and risk-appropriate repeat electrolytes and glucose, follow intake and fluid and clinical status, and assign review times, action thresholds, and an owner
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Correct: prospectivelycovers biochemical andbedside benefit/safety withaccountability.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Follow daily intake and weight with an owner, but defer electrolyte checks until symptoms develop
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Symptoms-only testing omits planned biochemical monitoring.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Arrange repeat electrolytes and glucose but omit fluid balance, intake, and clinical reassessment
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Laboratories alone omit delivered intake/fluid/clinical response.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Copy a stable outpatient schedule without adapting its intervals to initiation and high refeeding risk
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Stable community intervals cannot be applied unchanged to high-risk initiation.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: The agreed action, responsible clinician, measure and goal, review time, and escalation trigger
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Correct: action,owner,measure/goal,time andresponse trigger makefollowup executable.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: The action and measurement goal, with responsibility left to whichever team reads the note
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Leaves responsibility unspecified.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: The responsible clinician and a general monitoring instruction, without a measure or review time
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Leaves operational measurement and timing unspecified.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: The measurements and review date, with no decision planned if the goal is missed
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Leaves response to a missed goal unspecified.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Weekly weight for the stable patient and daily weight when fluid balance is a concern
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Correct: weekly otherwise,daily withfluidbalance concern;stability permits lessfrequent schedule.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Daily weight for the stable patient and weekly weight during new edema
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Reverses the risk-adjusted schedule.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Monthly weight for both patients from the first day of support
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Monthly from initiation ignores initial/risk monitoring.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Weekly weight for both patients regardless of changing fluid balance
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Weekly despite newfluidconcern ignores dailyweight indication.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Obtain baseline values and monitor magnesium and phosphate daily while refeeding risk is present, adapting frequency if instability requires it
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Correct: baselineplusdaily while refeedingriskpresent,frequency adapted ifneeded.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Repeat magnesium and phosphate only if symptoms appear because baseline values are normal
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Normal baseline doesnot justify deferring tests to symptoms.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Measure glucose regularly but defer magnesium and phosphate until the stable weekly schedule
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Glucose monitoring doesnot replace magnesium/phosphate surveillance.

priorIndividualChoiceReview.text: Measure magnesium and phosphate once weekly from initiation because there is no baseline deficit
priorIndividualChoiceReview.review: Stable weekly cadence isnot the stated risk-period cadence.
